name: advanced-ratelimit
description:
Rate limiting policy supporting multiple algorithms, multi-dimensional quotas, weighted rate limiting, flexible key extraction (including JWT/auth-context properties) with optional match conditions, and in-memory, Redis, and Redis-local-async backends. Supports fail-open behavior for Redis failures and provides comprehensive rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-*, IETF RateLimit, and Retry-After).

Key features:
- Multi-dimensional quotas: independent key/cost extraction per quota
- Auth-context key extraction: bucket requests by a JWT claim (e.g. app/client ID) already resolved by an earlier auth policy (jwt-auth)
- Conditional quotas: restrict a quota to requests whose key matches a pattern; non-matching requests bypass it entirely
- Multiple algorithms: GCRA (smooth) or Fixed Window (simple counter)
- Dynamic cost extraction: from request/response headers, metadata, or JSON body
- Weighted multipliers: e.g. prompt tokens @ 0.1, completion tokens @ 0.3
- Multiple concurrent limits (e.g., 10/second AND 1000/hour)
- Array-based key extraction, defaults to route name
- Three backends: in-memory (per replica), Redis (distributed, exact), or Redis-local-async (distributed, local-first with async reconcile, bounded overshoot)
- Shared Redis client pool per identical connection configuration within a process
- Optional TLS and mutual TLS for the Redis connection (CA bundle, server name, client certificate)
- Graceful degradation: missing key components warn, don't fail requests
- Atomic operations via Lua scripts (GCRA+Redis) or native Redis commands (Fixed Window)
